questionText:
A computer system with a word length of 32 bits has a 16 MB byte-addressable main memory and a 64 KB, 4-way set associative cache memory with a block size of 256 bytes. Consider the following four physical addresses represented in hexadecimal notation.

A1 = 0x42C8A4, A2 = 0x546888, A3 = 0x6A289C, A4 = 0x5E4880

Which one of the following is TRUE?
options: A1 and A4 are mapped to different cache sets.
A2 and A3 are mapped to the same cache set.
A3 and A4 are mapped to the same cache set.
A1 and A3 are mapped to the same cache set.
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the address bit partition
Block Size = $256\text{ bytes} = 2^8\text{ bytes}$, which gives a Block Offset of $8\text{ bits}$.
Cache Size = $64\text{ KB} = 2^{16}\text{ bytes}$.
Total Cache Lines = $\frac{64\text{ KB}}{256\text{ B}} = \frac{2^{16}}{2^8} = 2^8 = 256\text{ lines}$.
Number of Cache Sets = $\frac{256}{4} = 64 = 2^6\text{ sets}$.
Therefore, Set Index = $6\text{ bits}$.

Step 2: Map address bits to fields
Bits 0 to 7: Block Offset ($8\text{ bits}$)
Bits 8 to 13: Set Index ($6\text{ bits}$)

Step 3: Extract Set Index bits (Bits 8 to 13) for each address
- A1 (0x42C8A4): Bits 13–8 are `001000` (Decimal 8)
- A2 (0x546888): Bits 13–8 are `101000` (Decimal 40)
- A3 (0x6A289C): Bits 13–8 are `101000` (Decimal 40)
- A4 (0x5E4880): Bits 13–8 are `001000` (Decimal 8)

Both A2 and A3 are mapped to Set 40, making statement (B) TRUE.
